summary: Adaptive backpressure feedback loop in continuous batcher causing sporadic p99 latency regressions and timeouts
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (TalkStream Inc.) report intermittent p95/p99 spikes and request timeouts (504/ETIMEDOUT) during peak periods beginning 2026-03-10. Spikes are noisy and not correlated with single-model overload; symptom window is 10-40s where tail latency climbs sharply and request timeouts follow.

Impact:
- Several production endpoints for TalkStream experienced user-visible timeouts (~1-3% of requests during spike windows).
- Affected traffic routed to Redwood Dedicated pool in us-west.
- Customer business impact: degraded UX for live transcription product.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity: pool-dc-02 (us-west)
- Serving runtime: release v1.19.3
- Continuous batcher enabled with adaptive backpressure (feature flag: batcher.adaptive_backpressure=true)
- Traffic profile: many short streaming sessions (avg tokens/stream ~18) with sudden surge 2026-03-10 21:00-22:30 UTC

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Start a sustained stream of short requests (20–40 requests/s, 65% short streaming sessions).
2) Observe continuous-batcher linger_ms and batch_coalescing grow under backpressure.
3) Batches begin to accumulate cross-tenant micro-queues; KV cache warmups overlap with delayed batch flushes.
4) Tail latency climbs (p95→p99), some requests hit request timeout (client-side 30s) or server 504.

Expected behavior:
- Batcher should maintain stable linger and flush within configured SLOs; short streams should not cause multi-second linger growth or timeouts.

Actual behavior:
- Intermittent growth of batcher linger window (observed increase from ~6ms baseline to 120–450ms for affected microbatches), correlated with backpressure metric oscillations.
- Temporary increases in queue depth and waiting requests per worker.
- Several requests timed out after crossing client/server timeouts.

Logs / artifacts:
- Grafana panels: https://grafana.internal/redwood/dashboard/batcher-tail?from=2026-03-10T20:45:00Z&to=2026-03-10T22:45:00Z
- APM traces: https://apm.redwood/services/serving/runtime/trace/trace-20260310-21:12:43
- Support Slack: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02SUPPORT/p1678470000000
steps_to_reproduce: Generate sustained short-stream traffic (20-40 req/s) against dedicated pool-dc-02
Monitor continuous-batcher metrics: linger_ms, batch_size, inflight_requests, backpressure_ratio
Observe p95/p99 latency and 504/ETIMEDOUT counts during surge windows

comments: Priya Nambiar (support): Customer reported intermittent 504s during their evening traffic spike. Provided initial graphs and request ids.
Ethan Cole (engineer): Acknowledged and began telemetry capture. Noticed sustained rise in batcher.backpressure_ratio preceding p99 spike by ~30s.
TalkStream SRE (customer): Confirmed traffic surge pattern and that they did not change client timeouts. Provided additional trace ids.
Ethan Cole: Hypothesis: adaptive backpressure feedback loop causes linger inflation under many short streams; will instrument additional metrics and try temporary threshold change on a canary host.

Ethan Cole: Canary patch applied to pool-dc-02-worker-15 reducing adaptive threshold from 0.75 -> 0.65 at 2026-03-12T03:20Z. Early signal: reduced linger variance, p99 dropped to baseline in canary for 45m window.
Priya Nambiar: Informed customer of canary and asked for verification on their side. Customer reported improved behavior on canary-hosted traffic.
Ethan Cole: Preparing PR to add additional telemetry and a fallback mode that forces fixed linger for short-stream traffic classes. Marked follow-ups in backlog.
Priya Nambiar: Ticket will remain open until rollout and monitoring window complete; customer satisfied with temporary mitigation.
investigation_notes: Correlated p99 spikes with increase in batcher.backpressure_ratio and batcher.linger_ms volatility; pattern reproducible with synthetic short-stream traffic.

Observed that adaptive backpressure increases the target linger window when per-worker inflight_requests > worker_capacity * 0.7, but oscillation occurs because increased linger causes larger cross-tenant merges which further raise inflight counts.
KV cache warmup heatmap shows overlap: when new short streams arrive, KV misses spike and GPU kernels have higher variance leading to jittered service times that amplify backpressure signal.
Canary change lowering threshold to 0.65 reduced loop gain and prevented linger runaway on the canary worker for test surge windows.
No single-model overload detected; CPU/GPU utilization stayed below 70% during spikes — root cause appears algorithmic in batcher heuristics rather than raw capacity.
Related to recent runtime tuning change in v1.19.3 (batcher: introduce adaptive_backpressure with default gain=1.2). Investigating whether the gain parameter should be decoupled per-traffic-class.
Cross-referenced with SUP-15203 for intermittent timeouts during low QPS; similarities exist but this ticket shows feedback loop under surge of short streams.
Next steps: add per-traffic-class fixed-linger override, reduce default adaptive gain, add alerting for linger_ms variance and backpressure_ratio oscillation.
resolution: Mitigation applied: 2026-03-12 canary reduced adaptive backpressure threshold from 0.75 -> 0.65 for pool-dc-02-worker-15 which reduced linger volatility and restored p99 to baseline on canary traffic. Planned rollout: staged change across dedicated pool with follow-up monitoring for 48 hours. Long-term fix: implement per-traffic-class gain control and an escape hatch that forces a low fixed linger for short-stream class. Postmortem and config PR scheduled.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 03:20Z: Canary change confirmed, observed 70% reduction in p99 spike magnitude on canary host during test surge.
2026-03-12 13:00Z: Began staged rollout to remaining pool-dc-02 hosts with 10% ramp increments and monitoring window between ramps.
Follow-up items: create dashboard for linger_ms variance, add automatic rollback if p99 increases by >25% after change, add unit tests for adaptive gain stability (ticket INT-894).
follow_up_actions: Run 48h monitoring window post-rollout and report to customer
